boot.evidence: Guest boots are unchanged by this increment (no daemon boot path was touched beyond closing the inherited listener fd); the selftest daemons used by both suites supervise a bounded child and report phase=running, and the parity gate between the C and Rust daemons still passes with 7 identical lines.

own_log_rotation.evidence: lib/logs.sh rotates daemon.log / uml-console.log / bess.sock.gv.log by copy+truncate: the inode is preserved (verified: stat -c %i identical before/after) so a writer holding the file open keeps writing to the same inode instead of into a rotated generation. `up` rotates before every start, `uml4termux rotate` rotates on demand (per instance or --all), and retention keeps UML4TERMUX_LOG_KEEP generations (default 3) with the oldest dropped -- all asserted by tests/test-log-rotation.sh (14 checks, no daemon needed).

launcher_adapters.evidence: packaging/adapters/ ships systemd (uml4termux@.service), s6 (run + finish), plain (supervise.sh) and runit (run) adapters that all exec the SAME documented hook `uml4termux up --foreground`. Only the runit adapter mentions runit (static check over non-comment lines). The plain adapter is proven functionally, not just statically: it started the instance, then after a SIGKILL of the daemon it restarted with a NEW pid (15466 -> 15544) and readiness came back, and after a deliberate `down` (exit 0) it exited instead of looping.

orphan_child_kept_the_control_socket.evidence: Found THROUGH the adapter work: the C daemon created its listening socket without SOCK_CLOEXEC, so the supervised child inherited it. After a SIGKILL of the daemon an orphaned child kept the socket open -- clients still connected and then blocked forever, so a supervisor restart looked like a hang and `down` reported 'not running'. Fixed in src/uml4termuxd.c: socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC) plus an explicit close in both child branches (guest PTY and selftest); recorded as ok=false because it was a real product defect found and fixed in this increment, not a capability that was designed in.

foreground_up_did_not_register.evidence: Also found by the adapters: `up --foreground` exec'd the daemon without writing a registry record, so an instance started by any supervisor was invisible to `status`, `ls` and `down` (down fell back to the default runtime dir and reported 'not running'). Fixed: the record is written immediately before exec using $$, which IS the daemon pid after exec; the suite now asserts a supervisor-started instance can be found and stopped by name.

notes: Direction G4/G5 (docs/NEXT-STEPS.md). Rotation is pull-based: `up` rotates before each start and `uml4termux rotate` is the hook a supervisor tick or cron calls -- there is no in-daemon log rotator, which is deliberate (no C/Rust parity surface, no hidden threads).
known_limits_observed: continuous rotation needs a caller: `up` covers start-up, `uml4termux rotate --all` covers a supervisor tick or cron job
the s6 adapter's finish script relies on s6 passing (exit code, signal) as $1/$2; verified textually here, not against a live s6 supervisor
systemd-analyze verify runs in CI only (not available on the device)
